findings: Completion still extends query_events from upstream.take_query_events before testing events.is_empty. Upstream notices therefore drain even on cached/no-completion turns. The notice drain and the caller error/clock decisions remain outside the added empty check; per-event notices remain in the unchanged nonempty body.

Old empty completion allocated only Vec::new, skipped the event loop and returned it. New empty return has the same empty Vec and consumes/drops the input Vec once; spare input capacity is freed rather than leaked or newly retained. Option references to local/doctor have no owned destructor effects.

Every nonempty completion statement is byte-identical: timeout/upstream error counters, doctor/local-generation reply processing, recipient packet projection, duplicate/truncation notices, counters and response order remain unchanged. No unconditional post-loop action beyond returning responses was bypassed.

Upstream no_timer_or_socket_work guard, consume_releases and events.drain(..).collect return remain before the new helper exactly as before. Public signatures and Fn(&[u8],&Pending)->bool bound are unchanged.

All active polling body bytes are identical, including call deadline, scratch take/clear/reserve/restore, timers before and after socket work, poll EINTR/error handling, receive order, ignored-reply filter borrow and returned result. Moving the owned Fn into one private helper adds no invocation or state retention.
Each helper has one caller; all other product source and tests remain unchanged. This review reads committed Git objects, not the author working tree.
